content.value: Trace if and if-else statements, choose correct boundaries, and group conditional actions with braces.

An if statement evaluates a boolean condition and runs its body only when true. An optional else supplies the alternative action. In a simple if-else pair exactly one branch runs. Execution then continues with the statement following the entire conditional.

Braces group several statements into one branch. Without braces, only the immediately following statement is controlled. Distinguish one if-else chain from independent if statements: independent tests can both succeed, and a first body can change the value examined by a later test.
The condition is true at equality, so points becomes 12. The else body is skipped, and 12 is printed. With an initial value of 9, the condition would be false and the printed value would be 0.

A semicolon immediately after if (condition) makes the controlled statement empty. Indentation is for readers; braces determine grouping. Writing two if statements instead of if and else can cause both actions to occur.
Write a branch that assigns shipping = 0 when total is at least 50 and shipping = 5 otherwise. Test total values 49, 50, and 51, yielding 5, 0, and 0.
